title: How to organize the living room walkway
description:
Let anyone cross this room in the dark, carrying something, without touching anything.

This is The Floor and Circulation Path in the Living Room. About 15-30 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
A continuous clear route from the doorway past the sofa to the other exit, wide enough for two people to pass and for the vacuum to run through without being lifted. Rug edges lying flat on a grippy pad, no cord crossing the route, and nothing on the floor but furniture legs, the rug, and baskets pushed back against the wall.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Walk the route with a laundry basket and put every floor item in it: shoes, toys, yesterday's bag, the pile of post, the box that has sat beside the sofa for a month.
Straighten: Floor baskets go against a wall or under the side table, never in the route, and each one gets a named category so it does not turn into a bin nobody empties.
Shine: Vacuum the route, then move the sofa and chair legs and do underneath, because that is where pet hair and dust build up out of sight.
Safety: Curled rug corners, the lamp cord crossing the route and toys left in the dark are the three falls this room produces, and they happen at night to whoever is up first.
Standardize: Full width, always, and you check it by walking the route with a full basket in both hands rather than by standing in the doorway looking at it.
Sustain: When the vacuum comes out, anything still on the floor at the end goes into the basket and gets returned before the vacuum is put away, by whoever ran it.

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
The route from door to door stays clear at its full width.
